native_mcp_support.notes: The google-genai Python and JavaScript SDKs include experimental MCP client support (connects to MCP servers, calls list_tools, exposes tools to model). Only tools from MCP servers are supported — resources and prompts are not. Deep Research feature also has MCP support in preview. Marked medium confidence because it is still listed as experimental in the SDK.

skills_concept.value: Gems (Google AI Studio) and system_instruction parameter (API)
skills_concept.notes: Gems are customizable AI personas/experts in Gemini (consumer product) that persist system instructions across sessions. In the API, system instructions are passed via the system_instruction parameter. No equivalent to Claude Agent Skills or OpenAI Assistants as a first-class programmatic construct in the Gemini Developer API.

input_output_shared.notes: Gemini context window is a single shared pool; input + output draw from the 1,048,576 token window. Max output (65,536) is a separate generation cap, not a separate pool.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Google does not document a separate 'default' output cap distinct from the max; the documented limit is 65,536.

extended_context.notes: 1,048,576 (1M) is the standard GA window; no documented beta/extended window beyond this.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Pricing page explicitly labels output price as 'Output price (including thinking tokens)'. Token counting doc confirms thinking tokens appear in thoughts_token_count and are billed at output rate.

tokenizer_family.notes: Proprietary Gemini tokenizer (SentencePiece-based, closed). Token is approximately 4 characters; 100 tokens ~ 60-80 English words.

tokenizer_public.notes: Tokenizer weights are not publicly released; exact counts require the countTokens API.

tokenizer_access.notes: Use client.models.count_tokens() (Python/JS) or REST models.countTokens endpoint to get exact token counts before sending requests.

count_tokens_method.value: client.models.count_tokens(model='gemini-3.5-flash', contents=...) — Python SDK; ai.models.countTokens({model:'gemini-3.5-flash', contents:...}) — JS SDK; or POST /v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash:countTokens

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images are cropped/scaled into 768x768 pixel tiles, each tile = 258 tokens. Gemini 3 models support media_resolution parameter to control max tokens per image/frame.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio pricing uses a separate rate for input ($1.00/1M audio tokens vs $0.30/1M text tokens standard tier). Video converts at 263 tokens per second.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Gemini docs state: 'a token is equivalent to about 4 characters'. 100 tokens ~ 60-80 English words.

native_mcp.notes: Experimental MCP client in google-genai SDK (Python and JS). Queries list_tools endpoint of MCP servers and exposes tools to model. Only tool calling — resources and prompts not supported. Deep Research API also has MCP support in preview.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Documented as 'parallel function calling' — model can call multiple functions in a single turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: Hard API-enforced limit. Exceeded requests fail immediately with HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: 'tools[0].function_declarations: [FIELD_INVALID] At most 512 function declarations can be specified.' Confirmed from live error in Gemini CLI issue #19083 (Feb 2026) with model gemini-3-pro-preview. Applies across all functionDeclarations in the tools array. Not yet stated on the official function-calling doc page but is an enforced proto validation constraint.

max_tools_practical.notes: No Gemini-specific empirical limit documented. Official best-practices page recommends keeping active tool set to maximum 10-20 tools for accuracy. General practitioner consensus (~30-50) from Berkeley FCL work applies but not Gemini-specific data available.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Uses functionDeclarations array in a Tool object: {name, description, parameters (JSON Schema subset)}. Shape is similar to OpenAI function but passed as Tool.functionDeclarations[], not tools[].function.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Function declarations are included in the request and billed as input tokens. Use countTokens with the full request (including tools) to measure footprint.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No documented deferred/lazy tool loading mechanism in the Gemini API. Context caching can be used to cache static tool declarations and amortize the input token cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit for function/tool names in official Gemini API docs. Best practices page states: use descriptive names 'without spaces, periods, or dashes' (use underscores or camelCase). No maximum length stated. This differs from OpenAI's documented 64-char cap.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented maximum character or token cap on function description strings. Descriptions count toward input tokens (1M window limit applies). Best practices: be clear and detailed; provide examples. No hard length cap published.

max_request_size.notes: Inline data (inlineData field in REST): max 100 MB per request payload. PDFs limited to 50 MB via inline method. External URLs: 100 MB per payload. For larger files use Files API (up to 2 GB per file, 20 GB per project, stored 48h). This is the HTTP payload cap; the token window (1M) is a separate, usually-binding ceiling for text+tool payloads.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-function-response size limit in bytes or tokens. Gemini 3 series supports multimodal function responses (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain inline in functionResponse parts). Size of tool results contributes to the shared 1M token context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling is supported — model can emit multiple function calls in a single turn. No documented numeric cap on how many may be emitted simultaneously. Results can be returned out of order; the API matches them via the function call id field (Gemini 3 always returns a unique id per function call).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No documented hard cap on tool-call/result cycles per conversation turn. Compositional (sequential) function calling is supported natively in Gemini 3 models and the Python SDK automatic function calling loops until no more function calls are made. No 'you've reached your tool-use limit' error analogous to Claude's documented per-turn cap.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented limit on number of simultaneous MCP server connections in the experimental google-genai SDK MCP client. The practical binding constraint is the 512 total functionDeclarations limit across all connected servers. The SDK accepts multiple MCP ClientSession objects passed as tools.

max_total_tools.notes: Same as max_tools_hard — the 512 limit applies to total functionDeclarations across all Tool objects in the tools array of a single request. This is therefore the aggregate cap for tools from all connected MCP servers.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: OpenAPI subset only for function parameters. Supported keywords (as of 2025-11 update for Gemini 2.5+ and Gemini 3 models): type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. NOT supported in older models (pre-2.5): anyOf, oneOf, $ref, default, optional. For ANY function-calling mode the API may reject very large or deeply nested schemas — official docs recommend simplifying by shortening property names, reducing nesting, or limiting function declarations if errors occur. No documented maximum nesting depth or property count in official docs. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling (Notes and limitations section), https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionDeclaration
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Rate limits: Free tier 15 RPM / 1M TPM / 1500 RPD; Paid tier 2000 RPM / 4M TPM for Gemini 3.5 Flash (see ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits). Gemini 3.5 Flash has no long-context price tier. Context caching can amortize tool definition token cost (min TTL 5 min, storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour). Multimodal function responses (images, PDFs inline in functionResponse) supported for Gemini 3 series only. The 512 functionDeclarations limit is an API proto validation error (HTTP 400), not a soft warning.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: No first-class 'skills' or 'tools-as-persistent-capability-bundles' concept in the Gemini Developer API analogous to Claude Agent Skills or OpenAI Assistants. Gems exist in the Gemini consumer product (Google AI Studio), not exposed as a programmatic API.

skills_loading_model.notes: System instructions via system_instruction parameter are always-on per request. No progressive-disclosure or tool-triggered skills loading.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: System instructions are billed as input tokens on every request. No skills injection overhead beyond the system_instruction field. Context caching can cache static system instructions to reduce per-request cost.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System instruction tokens are billed as part of prompt_token_count input. No documented fixed overhead per request beyond the user-supplied system_instruction content.

prompt_caching.notes: Context caching supported. Cached reads: $0.15/1M tokens (standard tier). Cache storage: $1.00/1M tokens/hour. Cache min TTL: 5 minutes. Useful for caching large tool definition blocks or system instructions.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory feature documented in the Gemini Developer API (separate from context caching within a session).

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard paid tier, text/image/video input. Audio input: $1.00/1M tokens (different rate). No long-context price tier break for this model.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Includes thinking tokens. Standard paid tier.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Context cache read price. Cache storage also billed at $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

batch_discount.value: 50% off standard price (Batch API: input $0.75/1M, output $4.50/1M)

billing_unit.notes: Current billing is per-token (Gemini historically billed per-character in early 2023; per-token billing has been in place since at least Gemini 1.0 GA in Feb 2024 and confirmed for all current models).

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Audio input: $1.00/1M tokens (32 tokens/sec). Video input: 263 tokens/sec billed at text/video rate ($1.50/1M). Images: 258 tokens per tile (<=384px) or per 768x768 tile. Context cache storage: $1.00/1M tokens/hour regardless of modality.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Pricing page labels output column 'Output price (including thinking tokens)'. Thinking tokens are billed as output at $9.00/1M standard.

models.notes: Gemini 3.5 Flash is the flagship stable GA model as of June 2026, positioned for agentic sub-agent deployment. Supports Thinking mode (configurable). Priority inference tier available ($2.70/$16.20 per 1M in/out). Flex inference available at batch-equivalent pricing.

input_output_shared.notes: Single shared pool; output cap (65,536) is a generation limit, not a separate pool.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No separate default vs max distinction documented by Google.

extended_context.notes: 1M is the standard GA window; no documented beta/extended window.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Supports Thinking mode. Pricing labels output as 'Output price (including thinking tokens)'.

tokenizer_family.notes: Same proprietary Gemini tokenizer family as all Gemini models. ~4 chars/token.

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images tiled at 768x768 pixels, each tile = 258 tokens.

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio billed at higher rate: $0.50/1M tokens vs $0.25/1M for text.

native_mcp.notes: Experimental SDK-level MCP client support applies to all Gemini models including Flash-Lite.

max_tools_hard.notes: Same API-level proto constraint as all Gemini models: 512 total functionDeclarations per request. Error: INVALID_ARGUMENT 'At most 512 function declarations can be specified.'

max_tools_practical.notes: No Gemini Flash-Lite-specific empirical limit. Being a lite model, degradation may occur at fewer tools than Pro-class models. Official recommendation: keep active set to 10-20 tools.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred loading. Context caching can offset repeated tool definition cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit. Best practices: no spaces, periods, or dashes in names.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented maximum length. Token budget (1M window) is the effective constraint.

max_request_size.notes: Inline data: 100 MB per request (50 MB for PDFs). External URLs: 100 MB. Files API: up to 2 GB per file. Same limits apply to all current Gemini models.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-function-response size limit. Tool results contribute to the shared 1M token context window.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling supported; no documented numeric cap on simultaneous calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No documented hard cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented MCP server connection limit. The 512 total functionDeclarations limit is the practical binding constraint across all connected servers.

max_total_tools.notes: Same as max_tools_hard — aggregate limit across all Tool objects in a single request.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: OpenAPI subset for function parameters. Supported keywords (Gemini 3.1 as a Gemini 3-series model): type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. ANY mode may reject very large or deeply nested schemas. No documented hard depth or property count limits. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Rate limits: Free tier 30 RPM / 1M TPM; Paid tier 4000 RPM / 4M TPM (see ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits). No long-context price tier. Context caching supported (cache reads $0.025/1M, storage $1.00/1M tokens/hour). Most cost-efficient model; designed for high-volume agentic tasks.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: Same as Gemini 3.5 Flash — no first-class skills API.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: System instructions via system_instruction parameter billed as input tokens. Context caching supported to amortize static instruction cost.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed overhead beyond user-supplied system_instruction content.

prompt_caching.notes: Context caching supported. Cached read: $0.025/1M tokens (text/image/video), $0.05/1M (audio). Cache storage: $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

memory_feature.notes: No persistent cross-session memory in Gemini Developer API.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard paid tier, text/image/video. Audio input: $0.50/1M tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Text/image/video cached read. Audio cached: $0.05/1M. Cache storage: $1.00/1M tokens/hour.

batch_discount.value: 50% off standard price (Batch API: input $0.125/1M text/image/video, output $0.75/1M)

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Audio input billed at 2x text rate ($0.50 vs $0.25/1M). Video at text rate. Image at text rate per tile (258 tokens/tile). Cache storage charged additionally.

models.notes: Most cost-efficient GA model in the Gemini 3 family. Designed for high-volume agentic tasks, translation, transcription, lightweight data extraction. Supports Thinking mode. Stable release; no longer preview.

input_output_shared.notes: Single shared pool. Output cap (65,536) is a generation limit.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No separate default vs max documented.

extended_context.notes: 1M is the standard window. No extended window documented.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking model; pricing explicitly includes thinking tokens in output price. 'Output price (including thinking tokens)'.

image_token_rule.value: Images with both dimensions <=384 pixels = 258 tokens. Larger images tiled at 768x768 pixels, each tile = 258 tokens.

native_mcp.notes: Experimental SDK-level MCP client applies to all Gemini models.

max_tools_hard.notes: Same API-level proto constraint: 512 total functionDeclarations per request. The GitHub issue was filed against gemini-3-pro-preview but the error is an API-layer proto validation applied to all models.

max_tools_practical.notes: No Gemini 2.5 Pro-specific empirical limit data found. The large 1M context window provides significant headroom. Official recommendation: keep active set to 10-20 tools. General practitioner guidance of 30-50 tools applies.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No deferred loading. Context caching can offset tool definition cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit. Best practices: no spaces, periods, or dashes in names.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No documented maximum length. Token budget is the effective constraint. Note: for Gemini 2.5 Pro prompts >200K tokens, input rate doubles from $1.25 to $2.50/1M — long tool descriptions accelerate crossing this threshold.

max_request_size.notes: Inline data: 100 MB per request (50 MB for PDFs). Same as other Gemini models. For Gemini 2.5 Pro, text+tool payloads are unlikely to hit the 100 MB limit before hitting the 1M token limit.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No documented per-function-response size limit. Tool results contribute to shared 1M token window. Watch for 200K token pricing tier: large tool results push total prompt over 200K and trigger 2x input pricing.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel function calling supported; no documented numeric cap on simultaneous calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No documented hard cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn. Compositional function calling supported natively.

max_connected_servers.notes: No documented MCP server connection limit. 512 total functionDeclarations per request is the binding constraint.

max_total_tools.notes: Aggregate limit across all Tool objects in a single request.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: OpenAPI subset. Supported keywords for Gemini 2.5 Pro (as a 2.5-series model with Nov 2025 schema update): type, nullable, required, format, description, properties, items, enum, anyOf, $ref, minItems, maxItems, minimum, maximum. Key additions vs older models: anyOf and $ref now supported (Gemini 2.5+, confirmed via Google structured-output announcement Nov 2025). ANY mode may reject very large or deeply nested schemas. No documented hard nesting depth or property count. Pricing has a long-context tier >200K tokens (higher rate) which may affect tool-heavy sessions. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling, https://ai.google.dev/api/caching#FunctionDeclaration
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Rate limits: Paid tier 1000 RPM / 2M TPM. CRITICAL PRICING NOTE: Prompts >200K tokens billed at $2.50/1M input (vs $1.25 <=200K) and $15.00/1M output (vs $10.00 <=200K). Large tool definition sets (512 tools) can easily exceed 200K tokens, triggering the higher rate. Cache storage also 4.5x more expensive ($4.50/1M tokens/hour) than Flash models. Context caching is especially valuable for this model to keep tool definitions in cache.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: System instructions via system_instruction parameter billed as input tokens. Importantly, Gemini 2.5 Pro has a long-context pricing tier: prompts >200K tokens are billed at $2.50/1M input (vs $1.25 <=200K). Large tool+system prompt payloads crossing 200K will incur the higher rate.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: No fixed overhead. Watch for the 200K long-context price tier break when system instructions plus tool definitions exceed 200K tokens.

prompt_caching.notes: Context caching supported. Cached reads: $0.125/1M (<=200K prompts) or $0.25/1M (>200K). Storage: $4.50/1M tokens/hour (higher than Gemini 3.x models).

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard paid tier for prompts <=200K tokens. LONG-CONTEXT TIER: $2.50/1M for prompts >200K tokens. This is a key distinction from the Gemini 3.x models which have no long-context tier.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard tier for prompts <=200K tokens. LONG-CONTEXT TIER: $15.00/1M for prompts >200K tokens. Includes thinking tokens.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: For prompts <=200K. For prompts >200K: $0.25/1M. Cache storage: $4.50/1M tokens/hour (higher than Gemini 3.x models).

batch_discount.value: 50% off standard price (Batch API: input $0.625/1M <=200K, $1.25/1M >200K; output $5.00/1M <=200K, $7.50/1M >200K)

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Same tokenization rules as Gemini 3.x. Long-context price tier (>200K tokens total prompt) applies to all modalities. Cache storage is $4.50/1M tokens/hour vs $1.00 for Flash/Flash-Lite.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Deep thinking model; thinking tokens billed at output rate. Pricing page: 'Output price (including thinking tokens)': $10.00/1M (<=200K prompt) or $15.00/1M (>200K prompt).

models.notes: State-of-the-art thinking/reasoning model optimized for coding, math, and complex STEM tasks. Notable long-context price tier: input doubles from $1.25 to $2.50/1M for prompts exceeding 200K tokens — significant for MCP-heavy sessions with many tool definitions. Context cache storage is also 4.5x more expensive than Flash models. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (preview status, not included as the 3rd GA model) has similar specs but is not yet stable.
